experiment: E14: layout of rendered UML3 views in CATIA Magic (user observation 2026-09-17: diagram elements overlap)
setup: Same 9 example views as E13. Run A: views as they are (no render). Run B: view usages with 'render asTreeDiagram' (asInterconnectionDiagram for the component view, asElementTable for the class table). Both runs call DisplayExposedElements.layout(result) and count intersecting sibling shape bounds.

predictions.claim: Run A: DisplayMode.toDisplayMode(view) is UNDEFINED for every view, because no view declares a rendering
predictions.observation: UNDEFINED for 7 views; the component view is NESTED (inherited from InterconnectionView) and the grid table UNKNOWN

predictions.claim: Run A: at least one view has overlapping sibling shapes after display and layout
predictions.observation: overlapping sibling shapes in 8 of 9 views (190 in the class diagram); SVG header texts all at one position

predictions.claim: Run B: the display mode is TREE for asTreeDiagram views and NESTED for asInterconnectionDiagram
predictions.observation: render asTreeDiagram gives TREE, asInterconnectionDiagram NESTED, asElementTable UNKNOWN

predictions.claim: Run B: no view has overlapping sibling shapes after layout
predictions.observation: rendering alone does not lay out: overlaps unchanged. Calling the diagram's default layouter (LayoutManager.getDefaultLayouter(diagram) = SysML2DiagramLayouter, layout(diagram, null)) inside the session gives 0 overlaps in all 9 views, rendered or not

furtherObservations: The rendering changes the content: TREE shows compact name and keyword boxes (enum literals, metadata values); UNDEFINED shows full compartments (doc, attributes, items, ends), so documentation dominates the diagram
Decision 2026-09-17 (user): UML3 provides both compact views (render asTreeDiagram) and detail views (full compartments)
